description: Indicates the direction of transmission congestion affecting this pricing node: IMPORT (node is import-constrained, positive congestion component), EXPORT (node is export-constrained, negative congestion component), or UNCONSTRAINED (no binding transmission constraint). Supports FTR/CRR portfolio management and transmission congestion hedging strategy.

Code identifying the Balancing Authority Area (BAA) or control area within which this pricing node is located, as defined by NERC. Used for inter-area settlement, OATT compliance reporting, and NERC reliability reporting.

The date and time when this LMP price record was first ingested and created in the Databricks silver layer data product, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and ETL pipeline monitoring.
reference: SOX Section 404; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the LMP price values (e.g., USD for US Dollar, CAD for Canadian Dollar for cross-border markets). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of all monetary price components in multi-currency market contexts.

Code identifying the specific RTO/ISO data feed, API endpoint, or file type from which this LMP record was sourced (e.g., PJM_DA_LMP, CAISO_RTM_LMP_5MIN). Supports data lineage tracking, feed monitoring, and troubleshooting of price data gaps or anomalies.

The energy component of the LMP in US dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh), representing the system-wide marginal cost of energy at the reference bus. This component is uniform across all nodes in the market and reflects the cost of the marginal generating unit dispatched to serve load.
reference: FERC OATT; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Duration of the settlement interval in minutes (e.g., 60 for hourly DAM, 5 for RTM 5-minute intervals, 15 for 15-minute RTM intervals). Enables correct MWh energy quantity calculations when multiplying power (MW) by interval duration.

The end date and time of the settlement interval for which this LMP is applicable, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Together with interval_start_timestamp, defines the precise settlement window. Used to validate interval completeness and detect gaps in price data.

The start date and time of the settlement interval for which this LMP is applicable, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). For DAM, this is typically the top of the hour; for RTM, this may be a 5-minute or 15-minute interval start. Foundational for interval-level settlement and congestion analysis.
reference: FERC OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Indicates whether a transmission constraint was binding during this settlement interval at or affecting this pricing node (True = binding constraint active; False = no binding constraint). A binding constraint causes non-zero congestion component values and is critical for transmission congestion management and FTR/CRR settlement analysis.

Indicates whether the operating date falls on a recognized market holiday as defined by the RTO/ISO or applicable tariff (True = holiday; False = non-holiday). Holiday periods typically follow off-peak pricing rules and affect demand response program eligibility and TOU rate calculations.

Indicates whether the RTO/ISO applied a market price cap or floor to this LMP during the settlement interval (True = price cap or floor was applied; False = price cleared within normal bounds). Price caps are regulatory limits set by FERC to prevent market manipulation. Relevant for settlement dispute analysis and regulatory reporting.
reference: FERC Order 719; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The total Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in US dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh) for this pricing node and settlement interval, as published by the RTO/ISO. Equals the sum of the energy component, congestion component, and loss component. The primary price used for wholesale energy settlement calculations.
reference: FERC OATT; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Version label or identifier assigned by the RTO/ISO to distinguish between different published versions of LMP data for the same operating interval (e.g., 'v1', 'v2', or a timestamp-based version string). Used alongside revision_number to uniquely identify the authoritative price record for settlement and audit purposes.

The RTO/ISO-defined load zone or pricing zone code to which this pricing node belongs. Load zones aggregate individual bus nodes for zonal settlement and load-serving entity (LSE) obligations. Used for zonal LMP analysis, capacity market obligations, and TOU rate design.

The marginal loss component of the LMP in US dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh), representing the cost of marginal transmission losses at this pricing node relative to the reference bus. Reflects the incremental cost of delivering an additional MWh to this node accounting for line losses.
reference: FERC OATT; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The market operating day (yyyy-MM-dd) as defined by the RTO/ISO, which may differ from the calendar date for intervals near midnight due to market day boundary conventions. Used for market settlement period alignment and day-ahead vs. real-time reconciliation.

Identifies whether this LMP was published in the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or the Real-Time Market (RTM). DAM prices are forward-looking hourly prices cleared the day before delivery; RTM prices are five-minute or hourly prices cleared during the operating hour. Critical for settlement calculations and hedging analysis.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The calendar date (yyyy-MM-dd) of the operating day to which this LMP belongs. Used for daily aggregation, settlement period alignment, and day-ahead vs. real-time comparison reporting. Derived from interval_start_timestamp but stored explicitly for query performance.

The hour ending (HE) of the operating day (1–24) to which this settlement interval belongs. Standard RTO/ISO convention for identifying the delivery hour. Used for hourly aggregation, TOU rate alignment, and peak/off-peak classification.

Classification of the settlement interval into a peak period category based on the applicable tariff or market definition: ON_PEAK (high-demand hours, typically weekday daytime), OFF_PEAK (low-demand hours, nights and weekends), SUPER_PEAK (highest demand hours for CPP or TOU rates), or SHOULDER (transitional hours). Used for TOU rate analysis, demand response program evaluation, and IRP resource adequacy studies.
reference: FERC OATT; PUC Tariff; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Type of price cap or floor applied to this LMP when is_price_cap_applied is True. OFFER_CAP indicates the offer cap was binding; PRICE_FLOOR indicates the minimum price floor was applied; SCARCITY_PRICING indicates emergency scarcity pricing was triggered; NONE indicates no cap was applied. Used for market monitoring and regulatory reporting to FERC.
reference: FERC Order 719; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Data quality indicator for this LMP record as assessed by the utility's market data management or EMS platform. VALID = price passed all validation checks; SUSPECT = price flagged for review due to anomalous value; INVALID = price failed validation and should not be used for settlement; ESTIMATED = price was estimated due to missing source data; MISSING = no price was received for this interval.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Lifecycle status of this LMP price record indicating its settlement finality. PRELIMINARY prices are published shortly after the interval; FINAL prices are the binding settlement values after RTO/ISO validation; REVISED prices reflect corrections to previously published values; ESTIMATED prices are used when actual data is unavailable. Drives which records are used in financial settlement.

The date and time when the RTO/ISO officially published or released this LMP price record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Represents the business event time of price publication. Used to track data latency, validate timeliness of price feeds, and support audit trails for settlement disputes.

Sequential revision number assigned by the RTO/ISO or the utility's MDMS/market system to track successive corrections to a published LMP for the same pnode and interval. A value of 0 or 1 indicates the initial publication; higher values indicate subsequent revisions. Used to identify the most current authoritative price for settlement.

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Code
description: Code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) that published this LMP. Determines the market rules, settlement procedures, and tariff framework applicable to this price record. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|CAISO|MISO|NYISO|ISONE|ERCOT|SPP — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC Order 2000; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Seasonal classification of the operating date for this LMP record (SUMMER, WINTER, SPRING, FALL) based on the utility's or RTO/ISO's tariff-defined seasonal boundaries. Used for seasonal price analysis, capacity market seasonal obligations, and IRP resource adequacy modeling.
reference: FERC OATT; PUC Tariff; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Identifies the settlement billing period in which this LMP is used: INITIAL (first pass settlement shortly after the operating day), FINAL (binding settlement after all data is validated, typically 60 days post-operating day), or RESETTLEMENT (corrected settlement due to data errors or disputes). Determines which price version is used in financial settlement statements.

The native record identifier assigned by the source RTO/ISO market system or the utility's market data management platform (e.g., ABB or GE Energy Management System, or the RTO/ISO API response record ID). Enables traceability back to the originating system for audit, reconciliation, and dispute resolution purposes.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; SOX Section 404

description: The date and time when this LMP price record was last modified in the Databricks silver layer, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Updated when price revisions, quality flag changes, or settlement period reclassifications are applied. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Primary key for market_zone
Reference to the Balancing Authority responsible for maintaining load-resource balance and reliability in this zone.
Self-referencing FK on market_zone (parent_market_zone_id)
Reference to a parent or aggregate market zone if this zone is a sub-zone within a larger market area. Null for top-level zones.
Reference to the primary Load Serving Entity responsible for serving load in this zone, if applicable.
The specific pricing node or location identifier within the RTO/ISO system where Locational Marginal Price (LMP) is calculated for this zone.
Reference to the RTO or ISO that administers this market zone (e.g., PJM, NYISO, CAISO, MISO, ISO-NE, SPP, ERCOT).
The ancillary services region this zone belongs to for procurement of regulation, spinning reserves, non-spinning reserves, and operating reserves.
Indicates whether this zone participates in capacity market auctions and has capacity obligations (True) or is energy-only (False).
Historical metric indicating the frequency of transmission congestion events in this zone, used for risk assessment and hedging strategy. Scale 0-100.
Timestamp when this market zone record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether this zone participates in day-ahead market operations (True) or is real-time only (False).
Date when this market zone definition ceased to be effective, if applicable. Null for currently active zones.
Date when this market zone definition became effective and began being used for market operations and settlement.
External reference code or identifier used by the RTO/ISO or other market systems to identify this zone in data exchanges and settlement files.
Indicates whether Financial Transmission Rights or Congestion Revenue Rights are available for hedging congestion costs in this zone (True/False).
Textual description of the geographic boundaries of this market zone, including states, counties, or transmission substations that define the zone perimeter.
Total installed generation capacity within this zone in megawatts, representing the aggregate nameplate capacity of all generation resources.
Timestamp when this market zone record was most recently modified.
Method used to calculate the Locational Marginal Price for this zone: nodal (specific location), zonal (area average), hub average (multiple node average), or weighted average (load-weighted).
Average transmission loss factor applied to energy transactions in this zone, representing the percentage of energy lost in transmission (e.g., 0.02 for 2% loss).
Number of registered market participants (generators, load serving entities, traders) actively transacting in this zone.
Additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to this market zone, including operational considerations or historical context.
Historical or forecasted peak load for this zone in megawatts, used for capacity planning and resource adequacy assessments.
Indicates whether this zone participates in real-time market operations (True) or is day-ahead only (False).
Indicates whether this zone is designated as a Renewable Energy Zone with special interconnection or transmission rules for renewable generation (True/False).
Required planning reserve margin for this zone expressed as a percentage above peak load, mandated by the RTO/ISO or reliability coordinator.
Standard settlement interval duration in minutes for this zone (typically 5, 15, or 60 minutes depending on RTO/ISO rules).
Current operational status of the market zone: active (currently in use), inactive (temporarily suspended), pending (awaiting activation), or retired (permanently decommissioned).
Standard time zone abbreviation for this market zone (e.g., EST, CST, PST, MST) used for scheduling and settlement timestamps.
Identifier for the transmission constraint area or congestion zone that this market zone belongs to, used for managing grid congestion and calculating congestion charges.
Primary transmission voltage level in kilovolts for this market zone (e.g., 138, 230, 345, 500 kV).
Externally-recognized unique code for the market zone as defined by the RTO/ISO (e.g., ZONE_A, PJM_WEST, NYISO_J). Used in market bids, schedules, and settlement reports.
Human-readable name of the market zone (e.g., Western Hub, New York City, Northern Illinois).

Classification of the market zone indicating its primary function: load zone (demand aggregation), generation zone (supply aggregation), hub (pricing node), interface (interconnection point), or aggregate (composite zone).
Unique surrogate identifier for each market participant registration record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Serves as the primary key for this entity.
Indicates whether the utility is authorized to offer ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, reactive power) in the RTO/ISO market under this registration.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; NERC Reliability Standards; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Indicates whether the utility is authorized to participate in the capacity market (e.g., PJM RPM, MISO Planning Resource Auction) under this registration. True if authorized for capacity obligations and auctions.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

description: The total collateral amount in US dollars required by the RTO/ISO to cover the utility's market exposure under this registration. Determined by the RTO/ISO based on credit rating, market activity, and unsecured credit limits.
reference: RTO/ISO Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: The timestamp when this participant registration record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver Layer record management.
reference: SOX Section 404; FERC Record Retention Requirements

description: The credit rating assigned by the credit rating agency to the utility entity for purposes of satisfying RTO/ISO collateral and credit requirements. Determines unsecured credit limits and collateral posting obligations in the market.
reference: RTO/ISO Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: The credit rating agency that issued the credit rating used to satisfy the RTO/ISO credit and collateral requirements for market participation. RTO/ISOs require participants to demonstrate creditworthiness.
reference: RTO/ISO Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Indicates whether the utility is authorized to submit bids and offers in the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) under this registration. Supports scheduling and financial settlement for next-day energy positions.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Trade name or doing-business-as name used by the utility in market operations, if different from the legal entity name. May appear on market communications and RTO/ISO portals.

The date on which the market participant registration became effective and the utility was authorized to participate in the RTO/ISO market. Aligns with the RTO/ISO acceptance date and FERC authorization.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Indicates whether the utility is authorized to participate in the energy market (Day-Ahead Market and Real-Time Market) under this registration. True if authorized for energy bids and offers.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The date on which FERC granted market-based rate authority to the utility under the referenced docket number. Establishes the legal basis for wholesale energy market participation.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; 18 CFR Part 35

description: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket number associated with the utility's market-based rate authorization. Format follows FERC docket numbering convention (e.g., ER22-1234-000). Required for FERC compliance, rate case management, and regulatory reporting.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; 18 CFR Part 35

business_glossary_term: FERC Market-Based Rate (MBR) Authorization Expiration Date
description: The date on which the FERC market-based rate authorization expires and must be renewed. Null if the authorization is indefinite. Supports regulatory compliance monitoring and renewal workflow triggers.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; 18 CFR Part 35

description: Indicates whether the utility is authorized to hold and trade Financial Transmission Rights (FTRs) in the RTO/ISO market under this registration. FTRs are used to hedge against congestion costs in LMP-based markets.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff

business_glossary_term: Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) Resource Adequacy Flag
description: Indicates whether this market participant registration is associated with resource adequacy obligations under the utility's Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). True if the registration supports IRP-tracked capacity commitments.
reference: State PUC IRP Requirements; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

description: The date on which the market participant registration was most recently amended or updated with the RTO/ISO or FERC. Tracks the currency of the registration and triggers compliance review workflows.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The full legal name of the utility entity as registered with the RTO/ISO and on file with FERC. Must match the name on the FERC market-based rate authorization and RTO/ISO membership agreement.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; FERC Form 1

description: The RTO/ISO-designated load zone associated with the utility's load-serving entity registration. Determines the applicable zonal LMP for load settlement and capacity market obligations. Applicable when participant_type includes load_serving_entity.

The geographic market region or zone within the RTO/ISO footprint where the utility is registered to participate (e.g., PJM-WEST, MISO-Central, CAISO-NP15). Relevant for Locational Marginal Price (LMP) settlement and capacity market zone assignments.
The date on which the utility executed the RTO/ISO membership or participation agreement. Establishes the contractual start of the market relationship.
reference: RTO/ISO Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: The agreement or contract number assigned by the RTO/ISO for the utility's membership or participation agreement. Serves as the binding contractual reference for market participation rights and obligations.
reference: RTO/ISO Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Comma-separated list of NERC functional entity registration codes applicable to this participant (e.g., BA=Balancing Authority, TO=Transmission Owner, GO=Generator Owner, LSE=Load-Serving Entity, DP=Distribution Provider). Supports NERC compliance reporting and reliability standard applicability determination.
reference: NERC Rules of Procedure; NERC Reliability Standards

description: The unique identifier assigned by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) to the utility as a registered reliability entity (e.g., Transmission Operator, Balancing Authority, Generator Operator). Links market participation to NERC reliability compliance obligations.
reference: NERC Rules of Procedure; NERC Reliability Standards

business_glossary_term: Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) Filing Date
description: The date on which the utility filed its Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) with FERC, establishing the terms and conditions for transmission service. Relevant for transmission owner registrations.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 890; 18 CFR Part 35

description: Classification of the utility's role in the wholesale energy market as registered with the RTO/ISO. Determines which market products and services the participant is authorized to transact. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: load_serving_entity|generator_owner|transmission_owner|marketer|power_marketer|distribution_utility|combined_utility — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Email address of the primary contact person responsible for market operations and RTO/ISO communications under this registration. Used for regulatory correspondence, market notices, and settlement dispute communications.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Full name of the primary contact person at the utility responsible for market operations and RTO/ISO communications under this registration. Used for regulatory correspondence and RTO/ISO notifications.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Phone number of the primary contact person responsible for market operations and RTO/ISO communications under this registration.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The REC tracking registry or program in which the utility is enrolled under this market registration for tracking and retiring Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) to demonstrate RPS compliance (e.g., GATS, M-RETS, WREGIS, NEPOOL GIS). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GATS|MRETS|WREGIS|NEPOOL-GIS|PJM-GATS|ERCOT-REC|NAR — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: State PUC RPS Regulations; DOE Renewable Energy Standards; EPA Green Power Partnership

description: Free-text field for capturing supplementary information about the market participant registration, including special conditions, regulatory caveats, pending amendments, or operational notes relevant to market compliance and operations.

Current lifecycle status of the market participant registration with the RTO/ISO. Active indicates full market participation rights; suspended indicates temporary restriction; terminated indicates the registration has been withdrawn or revoked.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Email address of the regulatory affairs contact responsible for FERC filings and compliance activities associated with this market registration.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; 18 CFR Part 35

description: Full name of the regulatory affairs contact responsible for FERC filings, rate case management, and PUC compliance activities associated with this market registration. May differ from the primary market operations contact.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; 18 CFR Part 35

description: Indicates whether this market participant registration is associated with Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance activities, including Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) tracking and procurement.
reference: State PUC RPS Regulations; DOE Renewable Energy Standards

description: Indicates whether the utility is authorized to participate in the Real-Time Market (RTM) under this registration. Supports real-time dispatch, imbalance settlement, and deviation management.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Standardized short code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization or Independent System Operator with which this registration is held. Used as a denormalized reference for reporting and filtering without requiring a join to the RTO/ISO reference table. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|MISO|CAISO|ERCOT|NYISO|ISO-NE|SPP — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

The unique participant identifier assigned by the specific RTO/ISO to the utility as a registered market participant. This is the externally-known business identifier used in all market communications, bid submissions, and settlement statements with the RTO/ISO (e.g., PJM participant ID, CAISO SCID). Essential for FERC compliance and market operations.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The U.S. state(s) in which the utility holds a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) and is subject to state Public Utility Commission (PUC) jurisdiction. Relevant for aligning market participation with state-level regulatory obligations and IRP requirements.

The date on which the market participant registration was terminated or is scheduled to terminate. Null for active, open-ended registrations. Used for historical tracking and FERC compliance reporting.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: The maximum unsecured credit limit in US dollars extended by the RTO/ISO to the utility under this registration, based on credit rating and financial standing. Amounts above this limit require collateral posting.
reference: RTO/ISO Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: The timestamp when this participant registration record was most recently updated in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Section 404; FERC Record Retention Requirements

description: Indicates whether the utility is authorized to submit virtual bids (increment offers / decrement bids) in the Day-Ahead Market under this registration. Virtual bidding is used for financial arbitrage between DAM and RTM prices.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Power Purchase Agreement contract record in the wholesale energy market data product. Primary key for the ppa_contract entity.

Foreign key linking to regulatory.commission_order. Business justification: PPAs approved via commission orders. Links power purchase agreements to their regulatory approval orders for authorization tracking and compliance verification.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: PPAs are managed by specific business units (generation group, wholesale trading desk) with P&L responsibility. Cost center assignment enables profitability analysis, budget tracking, and performance

Foreign key linking to regulatory.cost_recovery_mechanism. Business justification: PPA costs recovered through purchased power cost adjustment mechanisms. Links specific power purchase agreements to their regulatory cost recovery riders for tariff rate calculation.

Reference to the specific generation asset or resource (power plant, renewable facility, or DER portfolio) that is the source of energy supply under this Power Purchase Agreement. Applicable for unit-contingent and tolling contracts.
reference: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: PPA revenue and expense must post to specific GL accounts for FERC Form 1 reporting and GAAP financial statements. Essential for revenue recognition, expense matching, and regulatory compliance in uti
Reference to the FERC-filed interconnection agreement governing the physical grid connection of the contracted generation resource. Required for unit-contingent and tolling PPAs.
Reference to the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) resource portfolio to which this Power Purchase Agreement is assigned. Supports IRP resource adequacy analysis and long-term supply planning.
reference: State PUC IRP Requirements; NARUC IRP Guidelines

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: PPA costs are major components of utility rate cases for cost recovery. Links wholesale power purchase agreements to rate proceedings for revenue requirement determination and tariff approval.

Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Power purchase agreements require regulatory approval and oversight. Links PPA to its regulatory proceeding for approval tracking, prudency review, and cost recovery authorization in utility operation

Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: PPAs for generation services often executed with vendors who provide equipment, O&M, or tolling services. Links contract management to vendor performance evaluation, insurance tracking, and consolidat
Reference to the wholesale market counterparty (seller or buyer) that is party to this Power Purchase Agreement. Links to the market counterparty master record.

Indicates whether ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support) are included in the scope of this Power Purchase Agreement in addition to energy and capacity.

Expected annual energy delivery volume in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) under this Power Purchase Agreement. Used for annual budget planning, FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause) forecasting, and regulatory reporting.
reference: FERC Order 888; State PUC Regulatory Reporting

description: Frequency at which financial settlement invoices are generated under this Power Purchase Agreement. Drives integration with SAP S/4HANA accounts payable/receivable and billing cycles.
reference: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; GAAP Revenue Recognition

description: Indicates whether the contracted resource qualifies for capacity market obligations under the applicable RTO/ISO capacity market (e.g., PJM RPM, MISO Planning Resource Auction). True if eligible; False if energy-only.
reference: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

business_glossary_term: Capacity Price per Megawatt (MW) per Month
description: Contracted capacity payment in USD per MW per month for capacity-inclusive Power Purchase Agreements. Reflects the resource adequacy value of the contracted capacity. Null for energy-only contracts.
reference: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

description: Human-readable descriptive name of the Power Purchase Agreement, typically including the counterparty name and project name (e.g., 'Sunrise Solar Farm PPA'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and regulatory filings.

Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the Power Purchase Agreement, used in counterparty communications, FERC filings, and ERP contract management. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA contract management module.
reference: FERC Order 888; SAP S/4HANA Contract Management

description: Current lifecycle state of the Power Purchase Agreement. Draft indicates the contract is under negotiation; pending_approval awaits FERC or internal authorization; active means the contract is in force; suspended indicates a temporary halt; terminated reflects early cancellation; expired reflects natural end-of-term.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

description: Total duration of the Power Purchase Agreement expressed in years. Used for IRP long-term resource planning, AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) calculations, and CAPEX amortization analysis.
reference: FERC Order 888; GAAP ASC 842 Lease Accounting

description: Classification of the Power Purchase Agreement by pricing and delivery structure. Fixed-price contracts lock in a set $/MWh rate; index-linked contracts float with market indices (e.g., LMP); tolling agreements grant the buyer dispatch rights over a generation asset; unit-contingent contracts tie delivery to a specific generating unit's output; heat-rate contracts price energy relative to a fuel heat rate. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fixed_price|index_linked|tolling|unit_contingent|heat_rate|capacity_only — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
reference: FERC Order 888; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

description: Maximum contracted generation capacity in Megawatts (MW) that the seller is obligated to make available under this Power Purchase Agreement. Used in NERC resource adequacy assessments and IRP capacity planning.
reference: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; FERC Order 888

description: Total contracted energy volume in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) over the full term of the Power Purchase Agreement. Used for long-term supply portfolio management and IRP resource adequacy analysis.
reference: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

description: Timestamp when this Power Purchase Agreement record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking per SOX and FERC record-keeping requirements.
Dollar value of credit support or collateral posted under this Power Purchase Agreement. Used for counterparty credit risk exposure monitoring and financial reporting.
reference: FERC Credit Reform; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; SOX

description: Type of credit support or collateral arrangement required under this Power Purchase Agreement to mitigate counterparty credit risk. Relevant for SOX financial risk management and FERC credit requirements.
reference: FERC Credit Reform; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; SOX

description: Specifies which party holds curtailment rights under the Power Purchase Agreement. Buyer curtailment allows the utility to reduce scheduled deliveries; seller curtailment allows the generator to reduce output; mutual curtailment permits either party. Relevant for Demand Response (DR) and grid reliability operations.

Named electrical delivery point or pricing node where energy is transferred under the Power Purchase Agreement (e.g., RTO/ISO hub, busbar, interconnection point). Aligns with LMP settlement nodes in the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) and Real-Time Market (RTM).
reference: FERC Order 888; OATT (Open Access Transmission Tariff)

description: Calendar date on which the Power Purchase Agreement becomes legally binding and energy delivery obligations commence. Used in IRP resource adequacy analysis and long-term supply portfolio management.
reference: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

description: Contracted energy price in USD per Megawatt-Hour (MWh) for fixed-price Power Purchase Agreements. For index-linked contracts, this represents the base or floor price. Null for tolling agreements where pricing is fuel-cost-based.
reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

description: Calendar date on which all parties signed and executed the Power Purchase Agreement. Distinct from the effective date; used for FERC filing timelines and contract audit trails.
