Reference to the maintenance or construction work order (from Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) that generated this OPEX transaction. Enables linkage between O&M labor and materials costs and specific asset maintenance activities. Critical for distinguishing OPEX from CAPEX in rate case filings.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NERC FAC-003

description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the OPEX transaction. Tracks the transaction from initial entry through approval, posting to the general ledger, and potential reversal. Essential for SOX internal controls compliance and financial close processes.

Name or employee identifier of the individual who approved this OPEX transaction per the utility's delegation of authority matrix. Required for SOX internal controls documentation and financial audit trails. Populated upon transition to 'approved' or 'posted' approval_status.

Timestamp when the OPEX transaction received final approval in the ERP workflow. Distinct from created_timestamp and updated_timestamp; captures the specific lifecycle event of approval. Used for SOX controls testing and financial close cycle time analysis.

Approved O&M budget amount for the cost center and FERC account combination for the applicable fiscal period. Enables budget-to-actual variance analysis at the transaction level. Supports financial planning and rate case test-year budget justification.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

description: Timestamp when the OPEX transaction record was first created in the source ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Used for audit trail, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking in the Silver layer.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the transaction amount (e.g., 'USD'). Required for multi-currency ERP environments and FERC financial reporting. Utility operations are predominantly USD but may include CAD for cross-border transmission operations.
reference: ISO 4217; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Reference to the employee associated with this OPEX transaction, applicable for labor cost postings (direct labor, overtime, benefits allocations) originating from the payroll system (SuccessFactors or Workday). Null for non-labor transactions such as vendor invoices or fuel purchases.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 500-series (labor); GAAP

description: High-level classification of the operating expenditure type. Categories align with standard O&M cost-of-service study breakdowns used in rate case filings before state Public Utility Commissions (PUCs) and FERC. Labor includes direct and indirect employee costs; contractor_services covers third-party O&M contracts; fuel covers FAC-eligible fuel costs.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts account number to which this O&M expense is classified. Electric O&M accounts include the 500-series (Electric Operation) and 500-599 range; Gas O&M accounts include the 800-series (Gas Operation). Directly drives FERC Form 1 (electric) and FERC Form 2 (gas) O&M expense schedule reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201)

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Description
description: Descriptive label for the FERC Uniform System of Accounts account code (e.g., 'Account 501 - Fuel', 'Account 510 - Steam Power Generation Operation', 'Account 803 - Natural Gas Purchased for Resale'). Provides human-readable context for financial reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201)

description: The fiscal accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year in which this OPEX transaction is recognized. Used for period-end close, monthly O&M variance reporting, and regulatory test-year normalization.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

description: The fiscal year (four-digit integer, e.g., 2024) in which this OPEX transaction is recognized for financial reporting purposes. Aligns with the utility's regulatory fiscal year used in FERC Form 1/2 annual reports and rate case test-year filings.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

description: Utility functional area to which this OPEX transaction is attributed, aligned with FERC Uniform System of Accounts functional classifications. Used to allocate O&M costs between electric and gas operations and between generation, transmission, and distribution for rate case cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1/2 reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201); NARUC

description: Indicates whether this transaction was initially posted as OPEX but subsequently reclassified as a capital expenditure (CAPEX) following engineering or accounting review. OPEX-to-CAPEX reclassifications are common in utility accounting and are subject to regulatory scrutiny in rate cases.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

description: Indicates whether this OPEX transaction represents a fuel cost eligible for recovery through the Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) mechanism. FAC-eligible costs (e.g., natural gas, coal, nuclear fuel purchases) are tracked separately for regulatory pass-through rate adjustments filed with state PUCs.
reference: State PUC FAC tariff provisions; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 501

description: Indicates whether this OPEX transaction is includable in the utility's rate case cost-of-service study as a recoverable O&M expense. Transactions flagged as non-includable (e.g., lobbying costs, penalties, shareholder expenses) are excluded from the revenue requirement calculation per PUC and FERC guidelines.
reference: State PUC rate case guidelines; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC

description: Net total amount of the OPEX transaction after applying overhead allocations, adjustments, and any credits or reversals. Represents the final O&M cost recognized in the general ledger for this transaction. Used as the basis for FERC Form 1/2 O&M expense schedule line items.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

description: For reversal or correcting entries, the transaction_number of the original OPEX transaction being reversed or corrected. Enables audit trail linkage between original postings and their reversals. Null for original (non-reversal) transactions.
reference: GAAP; SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Dollar amount of indirect overhead costs allocated to this OPEX transaction using the utility's cost allocation methodology (e.g., labor-hour basis, direct-cost basis). Overhead allocations are scrutinized in rate case cost-of-service studies to ensure only appropriate costs are included in revenue requirement calculations.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC; PUC rate case guidelines

description: The date on which the OPEX transaction was posted to the general ledger accounting period. May differ from transaction_date due to accrual adjustments or late postings. Determines the fiscal period for financial statement inclusion.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

description: Internal project or WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) code from the ERP system to which this OPEX transaction is charged. Used for project-level O&M cost tracking, particularly for multi-year maintenance programs, storm restoration activities, and demand-side management (DSM) program cost tracking.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

description: The quantity of goods, services, or resources consumed in this OPEX transaction (e.g., labor hours, MCF of natural gas, MWh of fuel energy, units of materials). Used in conjunction with unit_of_measure for unit cost analysis and fuel consumption tracking for FAC filings.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; AGA; IEEE

description: The regulatory jurisdiction (e.g., 'FERC', 'CA-CPUC', 'TX-PUC', 'NY-PSC') under whose rate-making authority this OPEX transaction falls. Used to allocate costs between FERC-jurisdictional (wholesale/transmission) and state PUC-jurisdictional (retail distribution) rate bases in cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC (18 CFR); State PUC tariff provisions; NARUC

description: Indicates whether this OPEX transaction is a reversal entry (credit memo or correcting journal entry) that offsets a previously posted transaction. Reversal transactions are common for accrual reversals at period-end and for correcting misposted O&M costs.
reference: GAAP; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SOX Section 302/404

description: Classification of the originating document type that generated this OPEX transaction in the ERP system. Distinguishes between vendor invoices, manual journal entries, period-end accruals, payroll cost allocations, intercompany charges, and goods receipts. Used for financial audit and SOX controls testing.
reference: GAAP; SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this OPEX transaction originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer and enables source-system reconciliation during financial close. Primary sources are SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud for financial postings, with work order costs originating from Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SOX Section 302/404

description: Gross base amount of the operating expenditure in the transaction currency before any adjustments, discounts, or overhead allocations. Represents the raw O&M cost posted to the general ledger. Used for OPEX budget variance analysis and FERC O&M expense reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

description: The principal real-world business event date on which the operating expenditure was incurred or the cost was recognized. Used for period-end accruals, FERC O&M expense reporting, and rate case cost-of-service study period alignment.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

description: Free-text description of the operating expenditure as entered in the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Provides context for the nature of the O&M cost, such as 'Turbine blade inspection labor - Unit 3' or 'Natural gas fuel purchase - Peaker Plant'. Used in audit reviews and rate case cost justification.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SOX Section 302/404

description: Externally-known business identifier for the OPEX transaction as assigned by the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Corresponds to the document number or journal entry number used in financial reporting and audit trails. Supports FERC Form 1/2 O&M expense reconciliation.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

description: The unit of measure for the quantity field (e.g., 'hours' for labor, 'MCF' for natural gas volume, 'MWh' for fuel energy, 'EA' for each/unit of materials). Enables unit cost calculations and fuel consumption analysis for Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) regulatory filings.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; AGA; IEEE

description: Timestamp when the OPEX transaction record was last modified in the source ERP system. Tracks reversals, corrections, and approval workflow updates. Required for incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Silver layer.

Identifies whether this OPEX transaction relates to electric utility operations, gas utility operations, or common/shared utility costs. Required for cost separation between electric and gas rate bases in combined electric-and-gas utility rate cases filed with state PUCs and FERC.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201); NARUC

description: The invoice number provided by the vendor or contractor for this OPEX transaction. Used for three-way match (PO, goods receipt, invoice) in the procure-to-pay process and for SOX accounts payable controls. Enables traceability from the general ledger entry back to the source vendor document.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Primary key for organization
Primary street address of the organization's physical location. Used for regulatory filings and correspondence.
Secondary address information such as suite, floor, or building number.
Total approved budget for the current fiscal year in US dollars. Used for budget variance analysis and financial planning.
Reference to the employee or executive responsible for budget planning and variance management for this organization.
City where the organization is located.
Financial accounting code used to track and allocate operating expenses (OPEX) and capital expenditures (CAPEX) to this organization. Aligns with general ledger chart of accounts.
Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the organization is located.
Date and time when this organization record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for financial transactions associated with this organization. Typically USD for US-based utilities.
Accounting method used to depreciate capital assets owned by this organization. Regulatory method follows FERC-prescribed rates; other methods align with GAAP.
Detailed narrative description of the organization's purpose, responsibilities, and scope within the utility enterprise.
Date when this organization was closed or became inactive. Null for currently active organizations. Used for historical cost analysis and organizational change tracking.
Date when this organization became active and began accepting financial transactions. Used for time-based cost allocation and historical reporting.
Primary email contact for the organization.

Primary operational function of the organization within the utility value chain. Generation produces electricity; transmission moves high-voltage power; distribution delivers to end customers; customer service manages billing and support; corporate provides enterprise services; regulatory handles compliance and rate cases.
Indicates whether capital investments by this organization are eligible for inclusion in the regulatory rate base for cost recovery. Critical for CAPEX planning and rate case preparation.

Indicates whether this organization is subject to regulatory oversight and rate regulation. True for generation, transmission, and distribution organizations; false for unregulated competitive business units.
Date and time when this organization record was last updated. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Identifier of the legal entity that owns or operates this organization. Used for consolidation in GAAP financial statements and SOX compliance reporting.
Reference to the employee who manages this organization unit. Used for accountability and approval workflows.
Unique business identifier code for the organization used in financial reporting and cost allocation. Typically assigned by the enterprise resource planning system.
Numeric level in the organizational hierarchy where 1 represents the top level (enterprise) and higher numbers represent deeper nested levels. Used for roll-up reporting and consolidation.
Full legal or business name of the organization unit. Used for financial reporting, regulatory filings, and internal cost center identification.
Abbreviated name or acronym for the organization used in reports and user interfaces.

Classification of the organization entity indicating its role in the financial structure. Cost centers track expenses only; profit centers track both revenue and expenses; business units are strategic operational divisions; departments are functional groups; divisions are major organizational segments; subsidiaries are legally separate entities.
Reference to the parent organization in the hierarchy. Null for top-level organizations. Enables hierarchical cost allocation and financial consolidation.
Primary contact phone number for the organization.
ZIP or postal code for the organization's address. Format: XXXXX or XXXXX-XXXX.
Financial accounting code used to track revenue and profitability for this organization. Used in return on equity (ROE) and return on investment (ROI) calculations. Null for cost-only centers.
Regulatory body or commission with oversight authority over this organization (e.g., state public utility commission, FERC). Critical for rate case filings and compliance reporting.
Geographic region or jurisdiction served by this organization. Used for regulatory reporting and rate case cost allocation by service area.
Indicates whether this organization is within the scope of SOX internal controls testing and audit requirements. True for organizations with material financial impact.
Two-letter state or province code where the organization is located. Critical for regulatory jurisdiction determination.

Current lifecycle status of the organization. Active organizations are operational and can have transactions posted; inactive organizations are temporarily suspended; pending organizations are being established; closed organizations are permanently retired.
Federal employer identification number (EIN) or tax ID assigned to this organization for tax reporting purposes. Format: XX-XXXXXXX.
Unique surrogate identifier for the profit center record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key generated by the lakehouse ingestion pipeline from SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA module.
Self-referencing FK on profit_center (parent_profit_center_id)

Regulatory-approved return on equity percentage for this profit center as determined in the most recent rate case or FERC order. Used to calculate the allowed return component in cost-of-service studies and PBR performance tracking.
reference: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission); State PUC Rate Orders; NARUC

description: Regulatory and operational business segment to which this profit center belongs. Drives FERC-required segment reporting and ROE/ROI analysis by business unit. Values align with the utility's FERC Form 1 and state PUC segment reporting requirements: electric_generation, electric_transmission, electric_distribution, gas_distribution, unregulated.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Approved annual capital expenditure budget allocated to this profit center in US dollars. Used for CAPEX tracking, rate base calculations, and AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) accruals in regulatory accounting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

business_glossary_term: Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) Eligible
description: Indicates whether this profit center is eligible to receive Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC) from customers or developers. CIAC receipts reduce rate base and are tracked separately per FERC Account 271 and state PUC requirements.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (Account 271); State PUC CIAC Rules

description: SAP Company Code (BUKRS) representing the legal entity to which this profit center is assigned. Used for GAAP financial statement preparation and SOX compliance segregation. Maps to the utility's legal corporate structure.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI; GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles); SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

description: SAP Controlling Area (KOKRS) to which this profit center belongs. Defines the organizational unit within which cost and profit accounting is performed. All profit centers within a controlling area share the same fiscal year variant and currency.

Default cost center code associated with this profit center for overhead allocation and cost-of-service studies. Used in rate case preparation to allocate shared costs between regulated business segments per FERC and PUC requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Cost Allocation Guidelines

description: Timestamp when this profit center record was first created in the source SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA system. Used for audit trail, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the profit center's reporting currency (e.g., USD). Defines the currency in which profit center financial results are reported and consolidated.

Depreciation method applied to capital assets assigned to this profit center. Regulatory depreciation rates are typically set by PUC order and may differ from GAAP depreciation. Impacts rate base calculations and FERC account 403 (Depreciation and Amortization of Electric Plant).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; State PUC Depreciation Orders

description: Primary energy commodity handled by this profit center. Distinguishes electric utility operations from gas distribution operations for FERC Form 1 vs. Form 2 reporting, and for separate rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Form 1; FERC Form 2; AGA (American Gas Association); State PUC regulations

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Class
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts classification associated with this profit center (e.g., Electric Plant in Service accounts 301-399, Gas Plant accounts 101-199). Drives regulatory financial reporting on FERC Form 1 and Form 2.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1; FERC Form 2

description: SAP Fiscal Year Variant (PERIV) that defines the fiscal year calendar applicable to this profit center. Determines period boundaries for financial reporting, budget cycles, and FERC annual report preparation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; GAAP; FERC Form 1

description: SAP Functional Area (FUNC_AREA) assigned to this profit center, used to classify costs by business function (e.g., generation operations, transmission operations, distribution operations, customer service, administration). Supports FERC functional cost classification and CAPEX/OPEX segregation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: GL account assignment group that governs automatic account determination for revenue and cost postings to this profit center. Ensures correct FERC account mapping for regulated utility accounting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-CO; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Node identifier within the SAP profit center standard hierarchy (SETCLASS 0106) to which this profit center is assigned. Enables roll-up reporting across organizational levels for EBITDA and segment reporting.

Indicates whether transactions posted to this profit center are subject to intercompany elimination in consolidated financial statements. Critical for SOX-compliant consolidation and FERC affiliate transaction reporting.
reference: GAAP ASC 810; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); FERC Standards of Conduct

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this profit center record in the source SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA system. Supports change tracking, SOX audit requirements, and incremental data pipeline processing.
Extended description of the profit center providing full business context, including the scope of operations, regulatory segment, and reporting purpose. Corresponds to LTEXT in SAP CEPC.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
description: NERC reliability region (e.g., WECC, SERC, RFC, MRO) associated with this profit center's electric operations. Used for NERC compliance reporting and bulk electric system (BES) reliability cost allocation.
reference: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation); FERC Order 693

description: Approved annual operating expenditure budget allocated to this profit center in US dollars. Supports O&M cost tracking, rate case cost-of-service studies, and EBITDA reporting by segment.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP; State PUC Cost-of-Service Guidelines

description: Geographic or operational location code associated with this profit center, linking it to a specific generation plant, transmission substation, distribution district, or gas service territory. Used in GIS-integrated financial analysis and asset management reporting.
reference: ESRI ArcGIS; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; IEEE

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the profit center within the SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO-PCA) module. Used in journal entries, cost allocations, and regulatory segment reports. Corresponds to the PRCTR field in SAP table CEPC.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Grouping identifier used to aggregate profit centers for management reporting, EBITDA analysis, and regulatory segment reporting. Corresponds to SAP profit center groups (SETCLASS 0106) used in report painter/writer reports.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Human-readable short name of the profit center as maintained in SAP CO-PCA (KTEXT field in CEPC). Used in financial reports, dashboards, and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Current lifecycle status of the profit center record. Active profit centers accept postings; locked centers are frozen for new transactions; inactive centers are retired from use. Corresponds to the LOCK_IND and PRCTR_STATUS indicators in SAP CEPC.

Classification of the profit center by regulatory and operational type. Regulated centers are subject to PUC/FERC oversight and rate-of-return regulation; unregulated centers operate in competitive markets; corporate centers capture holding company costs; shared_services centers allocate common costs.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC regulations

description: Regulatory rate base value assigned to this profit center in US dollars, representing the net investment on which the utility is permitted to earn a regulated return. Used in ROE calculations and rate case cost-of-service studies filed with FERC and state PUCs.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Case Guidelines; NARUC

description: Indicates the regulatory jurisdiction governing this profit center's rates and operations. Federal indicates FERC jurisdiction (transmission, wholesale); state indicates PUC jurisdiction (distribution, retail); both indicates dual jurisdiction; unregulated indicates competitive/non-regulated operations.
reference: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission); State PUC regulations; NARUC

description: Employee identifier of the manager accountable for the financial performance of this profit center. Corresponds to the VERAK field in SAP CEPC. Used for accountability reporting and performance-based ratemaking (PBR) analysis.
Full name of the manager responsible for this profit center's financial performance. Sourced from SAP HR/CO integration. Used in management reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
Approved annual revenue budget for this profit center in US dollars. Used in ROE and ROI analysis by business unit, EBITDA reporting by segment, and variance analysis against actual revenues.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP; State PUC Rate Case Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Membership
description: RTO or ISO market area in which this profit center participates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT). Drives energy market cost allocation, LMP-based settlement, and OATT compliance reporting.
reference: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission); OATT (Open Access Transmission Tariff); RTO/ISO tariffs

description: Code used to map this profit center to a reportable segment under GAAP ASC 280 (Segment Reporting) and FERC segment reporting requirements. Enables aggregation of profit centers into disclosed business segments in annual reports and FERC filings.
reference: GAAP ASC 280 (Segment Reporting); FERC Form 1; SEC Regulation S-X

description: Identifier of the operational source system from which this profit center record was ingested (e.g., SAP_S4HANA_PROD, SAP_S4HANA_QA). Supports data lineage, multi-system reconciliation, and Silver Layer provenance tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; Enterprise Data Governance Standards

description: Indicates whether this profit center is within scope for SOX internal controls over financial reporting. SOX-relevant profit centers require documented controls, segregation of duties, and periodic management attestation.
reference: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 302 and 404; PCAOB Standards

description: Date from which this profit center is effective and available for financial postings. Corresponds to DATAB in SAP CEPC. Used to enforce temporal validity in period-based financial reporting and rate case cost studies.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Date through which this profit center remains effective. Corresponds to DATBI in SAP CEPC. A value of 9999-12-31 indicates an open-ended profit center with no planned deactivation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Indicates whether this profit center is designated to capture Work in Progress (WIP) costs for capital projects prior to asset capitalization. When true, costs posted here are subject to AFUDC accrual per FERC accounting requirements.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (Account 107 - Construction Work in Progress); GAAP ASC 835

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each budget record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Each record represents a unique combination of budget version, budget type, cost center, GL account, and fiscal year. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA CO-PA or Oracle ERP Cloud Budgetary Control module.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO-PA); Oracle ERP Cloud Budgetary Control

description: FK to finance.capex_project

Reference to the cost center responsible for this budget record. Cost centers represent organizational units (e.g., Generation Operations, T&D Maintenance, Customer Service) used for OPEX and CAPEX allocation in FERC Uniform System of Accounts reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SAP S/4HANA CO-CCA

description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: budget has fiscal_year and fiscal_period attributes. financial_period is the master for fiscal periods. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full period metadata (period dates, status, etc

Reference to the General Ledger account associated with this budget record. GL accounts are structured per FERC Uniform System of Accounts (e.g., Account 401 for Revenue, Account 500-series for O&M expenses, Account 100-series for utility plant CAPEX).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 980

description: FK to finance.profit_center

The proportional allocation factor (0.000000 to 1.000000) used to distribute shared or common costs across jurisdictions, functional areas, or cost centers in rate case cost-of-service studies. Derived from FERC-approved or PUC-approved allocation methodologies (e.g., plant ratio, revenue ratio, customer count).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Cost Allocation Methodology; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

description: The date on which this budget record received formal approval (yyyy-MM-dd). Marks the start of the authorized budget execution period. Used for SOX audit trail, board resolution documentation, and rate case filing timelines.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 270; PUC Rate Case Filing Requirements

description: Current workflow status of the budget record in the approval lifecycle. 'draft' indicates budget under preparation; 'pending_approval' indicates submitted for management or board review; 'approved' indicates authorized for execution; 'rejected' indicates returned for revision; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a revised version.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO); PUC Rate Case Filing

description: The total board- or management-approved budget amount in USD for this cost center, GL account, and fiscal year combination. Represents the authorized spending or revenue target. Used as the baseline for budget-vs-actual variance analysis and rate case test year cost-of-service calculations.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; FERC Form 1; SOX Section 302/404

description: Name or employee identifier of the executive or board member who formally approved this budget record. Required for SOX audit trail and internal control documentation. For CAPEX budgets, may reference the Capital Expenditure Committee or Board of Directors approval.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

description: The utility asset category for CAPEX budget records (e.g., Generation Plant, Transmission Lines, Distribution Substation, Gas Pipeline, Smart Meter/AMI, IT Infrastructure). Aligns with FERC plant account classifications for regulatory depreciation and rate base inclusion. Null for OPEX budget records.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (Electric Plant Accounts 301–399; Gas Plant Accounts 101–399); GAAP ASC 360

description: Classifies the nature of the budget record. 'opex' covers O&M operating expenditures; 'capex' covers capital expenditures for utility plant additions; 'revenue' covers projected rate revenues; 'depreciation' covers regulatory depreciation expense budgets; 'regulatory' covers rate case and compliance cost budgets. Aligns with FERC Uniform System of Accounts classification.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; PBR Target-Setting Guidelines

description: The timestamp when this budget record was first created in the source system or ingested into the Silver Layer lakehouse (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for SOX audit trail and data governance lineage tracking.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this budget record (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency reporting for utilities with cross-border operations or international PPAs. Typically USD for domestic U.S. utility operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; GAAP ASC 830 (Foreign Currency)

description: The annual regulatory depreciation rate (as a percentage) applied to CAPEX budget records for utility plant additions. Established by PUC-approved depreciation studies. Used to calculate budgeted depreciation expense for rate case cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1 reporting. Null for OPEX budget records.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Depreciation Study Approval; GAAP ASC 360

description: The date on which this budget record expires or is superseded (yyyy-MM-dd). For annual budgets, typically the last day of the fiscal year. For multi-year long-range plans, may extend 3–10 years. Nullable for open-ended rolling forecasts.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; FERC Form 1; IRP (Integrated Resource Plan) Filing

description: The date from which this budget record becomes effective and spending or revenue targets are active (yyyy-MM-dd). Typically the first day of the fiscal year or the effective date of a mid-year budget revision. Used for temporal budget validity tracking.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; FERC Form 1; PUC Rate Case Test Year

description: Identifies whether this budget record pertains to electric or gas utility operations, or a specific generation fuel type. Required for FERC jurisdictional cost separation between electric and gas operations, and for RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) compliance cost tracking.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1 (Electric); FERC Form 2 (Gas); RPS Compliance Reporting

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: The FERC Uniform System of Accounts account number (e.g., 401, 500, 101) mapped to this budget record. Required for FERC Form 1 annual report filing and rate case cost-of-service studies. Enables regulatory cost allocation between electric plant, O&M, and revenue accounts.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: The fiscal period (month number 1–12) within the fiscal year for which this budget amount is recorded. Enables monthly budget-vs-actual variance reporting and period-level financial planning cycles in SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; SAP S/4HANA CO-PA Period Accounting

description: The fiscal year to which this budget record applies (e.g., 2025). Used for annual budget cycle management, rate case test year identification, and multi-year capital program planning. Aligns with the utility's regulatory fiscal year as filed with the PUC and FERC.
reference: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 270; PUC Rate Case Filing Requirements

description: The business functional area associated with this budget record (e.g., Generation, Transmission, Electric Distribution, Gas Distribution, Customer Service, Corporate). Used for cost-of-service allocation in rate case studies and FERC jurisdictional separation of costs between electric and gas operations.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Cost-of-Service Allocation

description: Free-text narrative field for budget analysts to document assumptions, drivers, variance explanations, or special circumstances associated with this budget record. Supports rate case workpaper documentation and SOX audit trail requirements.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

description: Name or employee identifier of the manager or director responsible for this budget record (e.g., Director of Generation Operations, VP of T&D). Accountable for budget execution, variance explanations, and SOX attestation of financial controls for their cost center.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

description: Indicates whether this budget record is associated with a PBR (Performance-Based Ratemaking) performance target or incentive mechanism established by the PUC. True = linked to a PBR metric (e.g., SAIDI, SAIFI, customer satisfaction); False = standard budget record.
reference: PUC PBR Order; NARUC Performance-Based Ratemaking Guidelines

description: The budget amount allocated to the specific fiscal period (month) within the fiscal year, in USD. Supports monthly budget-vs-actual variance reporting and cash flow planning. The sum of all period amounts for a fiscal year should equal the approved_amount for annual budget records.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; SAP S/4HANA CO-PA Period Accounting

description: Identifies the financial planning cycle that produced this budget record. 'annual' is the primary year-end budget cycle; 'mid_year_review' is the formal mid-year reforecast; quarterly forecasts (q1–q3) are rolling updates; 'long_range' covers multi-year IRP and capital program planning cycles.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; FERC Form 1; IRP Filing Requirements

description: The actual expenditure or revenue recorded in the prior fiscal year for the same cost center and GL account combination, in USD. Used as a baseline reference for budget development, trend analysis, and rate case historical test year comparisons filed with the PUC.
reference: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 270; PUC Rate Case Historical Test Year

description: Indicates whether this budget record is designated as part of the rate case test year cost-of-service study submitted to the PUC or FERC. True = this record is included in the test year filing; False = standard budget record not designated for rate case use.
reference: PUC Rate Case Filing Requirements; FERC Form 1; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

description: The regulatory jurisdiction to which this budget record is allocated (e.g., FERC, State PUC name, Unregulated). Used for jurisdictional cost separation in rate case filings, FERC Form 1 reporting, and allocation of shared costs between regulated and unregulated business segments.
reference: FERC Form 1; PUC Rate Case Filing; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The natural key or document number from the originating source system (e.g., SAP CO document number, Oracle budget line ID). Used for data lineage, reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the ERP source system, and SOX audit trail.
reference: SOX IT General Controls (ITGC); Data Governance Lineage Standards

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this budget record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse. Typical sources include SAP S/4HANA CO-PA, Oracle ERP Cloud Budgetary Control, Hyperion Planning, or Anaplan for financial planning.
reference: Data Governance Framework; SOX IT General Controls (ITGC)

description: The timestamp when this budget record was last modified in the source system or Silver Layer lakehouse (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and SOX audit trail of budget amendments.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

description: The allowable percentage deviation between budgeted and actual amounts before a budget variance alert or escalation is triggered. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 10.00 for 10%). Used in monthly budget-vs-actual variance reporting and SOX internal control monitoring.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

description: Identifies the planning iteration of this budget record. 'original' is the board-approved annual budget; 'revised' reflects mid-year amendments; 'forecast' is the rolling latest estimate; 'long_range_plan' covers multi-year capital programs (IRP/CAPEX plans); 'supplemental' covers emergency or regulatory-driven additions.
reference: GAAP ASC 270; FERC Form 1; PUC Rate Case Cost-of-Service Study

description: The Work Breakdown Structure element code from SAP Project System (PS) or Oracle ERP Project module, used to track CAPEX budgets at the project or sub-project level. Supports AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) tracking and WIP (Work in Progress) capitalization per FERC accounting rules.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107 (Construction Work in Progress); GAAP ASC 835-3 (AFUDC)

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each capital expenditure transaction record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Internal Object Numbering; GAAP ASC 360

description: Reference to the authorized capital project or WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) element to which this expenditure is charged. Links the expenditure to the approved capital budget authorization.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PS (Project System); FERC Uniform System of Accounts

Reference to the fixed asset or asset-under-construction to which this expenditure will be capitalized upon project completion. Null while the project is in Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) status.
reference: Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo Asset Management; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

Reference to the vendor or contractor who supplied materials or services for this capital expenditure. Sourced from the ERP vendor master (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud).
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM (Materials Management); Oracle ERP Cloud Procurement

description: Reference to the work order (from Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) under which the capital work was performed. Connects the financial expenditure to the physical asset maintenance or construction activity.
reference: Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo Work Order Management

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Amount
description: The dollar amount of AFUDC accrued on this capital expenditure for the applicable period. Calculated as expenditure balance multiplied by the AFUDC rate. Capitalized to the asset cost basis and recovered through depreciation in rates.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 835-20; FERC Form 1

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Rate
description: The AFUDC rate applied to this expenditure for the period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.075 for 7.5%). AFUDC represents the cost of financing construction and is capitalized to the asset cost basis per FERC regulations and GAAP ASC 835-20.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 835-20; FERC Form 1

description: Reference number or identifier for the capital authorization document (e.g., Capital Appropriation Request, Board Resolution, or CPCN number) that approved this expenditure. Required for SOX compliance and audit trail.
reference: SOX Section 404; FERC CPCN Requirements; Internal Capital Authorization Policy

description: Name or employee identifier of the individual who approved this capital expenditure transaction. Required for SOX internal controls documentation and audit trail.
reference: SOX Section 302 and 404; Internal Capital Authorization Policy

description: High-level classification of the utility asset type being constructed or acquired. Drives FERC plant account assignment and depreciation rate selection. Values align with FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant categories.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 360

description: The approved capital budget amount for the project or WBS element at the time of this expenditure. Used for budget-to-actual variance analysis and capital spend tracking against authorized CAPEX.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1; Internal Capital Authorization Policy

description: Current capitalization lifecycle state of this expenditure. 'wip' indicates the cost is in Construction Work in Progress (CWIP); 'placed_in_service' indicates the asset has been capitalized to the fixed asset register; 'expensed' indicates the cost was reclassified as OPEX; 'reversed' indicates a correcting entry; 'pending_review' indicates awaiting capitalization determination.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107 (CWIP)

description: Timestamp when this capital expenditure record was first created in the source system or ingested into the Silver layer. Used for audit trail, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the expenditure amounts (e.g., USD). Power and Utilities operates primarily in USD; this field supports multi-currency ERP configurations and foreign contractor invoices.

Gross amount of the capital expenditure in USD before any adjustments. Represents the base cost charged to the CAPEX project for this transaction line. Used for CWIP balance tracking and budget variance analysis.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The actual calendar date on which the capital expenditure was incurred or the cost was recognized. This is the principal business event date used for CWIP balance reporting and period-end close.
reference: GAAP ASC 835-20 (AFUDC); FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Free-text description of the capital expenditure, including the nature of work performed, materials procured, or services rendered. Provides context for audit review, rate case cost justification, and asset capitalization documentation.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 404; FERC Form 1

description: Externally-known business identifier for this capital expenditure transaction, typically sourced from the ERP system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA document number or Oracle ERP Cloud transaction number). Used for cross-system traceability and audit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; Oracle ERP Cloud Project Costing

description: Classification of the nature of the capital expenditure. Drives cost allocation and capitalization treatment. Values: labor (internal workforce), materials (equipment and supplies), contractor (third-party services), overhead (allocated indirect costs), afudc_accrual (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction accrual), other.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 835-20 (AFUDC)

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account number (e.g., Account 310-399 for Electric Plant in Service, Account 107 for CWIP) to which this expenditure is classified. Required for FERC Form 1 regulatory reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: The fiscal accounting period (month number, 1-12) within the fiscal year in which this expenditure is posted. Used for monthly CAPEX tracking, period-end close reconciliation, and management reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI; Oracle ERP Cloud General Ledger; GAAP ASC 250

description: The fiscal year in which this capital expenditure is recorded. Used for annual CAPEX budget tracking, FERC Form 1 annual reporting, and year-over-year capital spend analysis.
reference: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 250; SOX Section 404

description: The physical or logical functional location code (from Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo, or ESRI ArcGIS GIS system) identifying where the capital work is being performed. Examples: substation identifier, transmission line segment, distribution circuit, gas pipeline segment.
reference: IBM Maximo Functional Location; ESRI ArcGIS Network Dataset; IEEE 1366

description: The vendor invoice number associated with this capital expenditure. Used for accounts payable matching, audit trail, and dispute resolution. Sourced from the ERP accounts payable module.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AP; Oracle ERP Cloud Payables; SOX Section 404

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether this expenditure qualifies for AFUDC accrual under FERC regulations and GAAP ASC 835-20. True if the expenditure is part of a qualifying construction project with a construction period exceeding the AFUDC threshold.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 835-20

description: Indicates whether this expenditure has been formally capitalized to the fixed asset register (True) or remains in CWIP or has been expensed (False). Used to filter capitalized vs. in-progress costs for balance sheet reporting.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Net capital expenditure amount after adjustments, credits, or reversals (expenditure_amount + tax_amount minus any credits). Represents the final capitalized cost contribution of this transaction to the project.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The date on which the constructed or acquired asset was placed in service and transferred from CWIP (Construction Work in Progress) to the fixed asset register. Triggers the start of depreciation and AFUDC cessation. Null while the project remains in WIP status.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; IRS Publication 946

description: The date on which the expenditure was posted to the General Ledger (GL) in the ERP system. May differ from expenditure_date due to period-end accruals or late postings. Used for financial period reconciliation.
reference: GAAP ASC 250; SAP S/4HANA FI General Ledger

description: Quantity of units (hours, units of material, etc.) associated with this capital expenditure. For labor expenditures, represents hours worked. For materials, represents units procured. Used for unit cost analysis and project cost benchmarking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PS; Oracle ERP Cloud Project Costing

description: Indicates the regulatory jurisdiction governing this capital expenditure for rate recovery purposes. 'ferc' for FERC-jurisdictional transmission assets, 'state_puc' for state-regulated distribution assets, 'both' for dual-jurisdiction assets, 'non_regulated' for unregulated capital.
reference: FERC (18 CFR Part 101); State PUC Regulations; NARUC

description: The utility service territory or operating division where the capital expenditure is incurred. Used for jurisdictional cost allocation in rate cases filed with state Public Utility Commissions (PUCs) and FERC.
reference: FERC Form 1; State PUC Rate Case Filing Requirements; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this capital expenditure record was sourced. Used for data lineage, ETL reconciliation, and audit trail in the Databricks Silver layer lakehouse.
reference: SAP S/4HANA; Oracle ERP Cloud; Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo

description: The native transaction identifier from the source operational system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA accounting document number, Oracle ERP Cloud expenditure item ID). Enables traceability from the Silver layer back to the system of record for reconciliation and audit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI; Oracle ERP Cloud Project Costing; SOX Section 404

description: Sales or use tax amount associated with this capital expenditure, if applicable. Capitalized taxes are included in the cost basis of the asset per GAAP. Reported separately for tax compliance and rate case cost-of-service studies.

Unit of measure for the expenditure quantity (e.g., hours for labor, each for equipment units, feet/miles for cable or pipeline, kVA or MW for electrical equipment). Used for unit cost benchmarking and project cost analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hours|each|feet|miles|kva|mw|lbs|tons|other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; IEEE Standard Units; AGA Measurement Standards

description: Timestamp when this capital expenditure record was last modified in the source system or updated in the Silver layer. Used for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and SOX audit trail.
reference: SOX Section 404; GAAP ASC 250; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Feed

description: The specific WBS element code within the capital project hierarchy to which this expenditure is charged. Provides granular cost tracking within a multi-phase or multi-component capital project.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PS (Project System); PMI PMBOK

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the capital expenditure project record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for the capex_project data product.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: capex_project has cost_center attribute (STRING). cost_center is the master for cost centers. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full cost center details (name, responsible_manager, func

Reference to the regulatory rate case in which this capital project's costs are included for rate base recovery. Links capital investment to the regulatory docket for cost-of-service studies and plant additions testimony.
reference: State PUC Rate Case Filing Requirements; FERC Rate Case Procedures

description: Cumulative actual capital expenditures incurred on the project to date, expressed in US dollars. Sourced from the ERP cost collection against the WBS element. Used for CWIP balance reporting, budget variance analysis, and capital program tracking.
reference: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Actual date on which the capital project assets were placed in service and transferred from CWIP to plant in service accounts. Triggers AFUDC cessation, depreciation commencement, and inclusion in rate base. Null until the project reaches in-service status.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 360

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Accrued Amount
description: Cumulative AFUDC amount capitalized to the project to date, expressed in US dollars. Represents the financing cost of construction capitalized per FERC accounting rules. Included in the total project cost and rate base upon in-service. Null if afudc_eligible is False.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 980-835

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Eligible Flag
description: Flag indicating whether this capital project is eligible for Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) accrual (True) or not (False). AFUDC represents the cost of financing construction and is capitalized to the project per FERC accounting rules. Eligibility is determined by project type, duration, and regulatory authorization.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 980-835

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Accrual Rate
description: AFUDC accrual rate applied to the project's CWIP balance to calculate the monthly AFUDC capitalization, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.075000 for 7.5%). Rate is set by the utility's regulatory accounting policy and approved by FERC or state PUC. Null if afudc_eligible is False.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 980-835

description: Asset class designation that categorizes the type of utility plant asset being constructed or acquired (e.g., Overhead Lines, Underground Cable, Transformers, Meters, Gas Mains, Buildings, IT Equipment). Aligns with Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo asset class hierarchy and FERC plant account groupings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overhead_lines|underground_cable|transformers|meters|gas_mains|buildings|it_equipment|generation_equipment|substation_equipment|vehicles — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Class

description: Date on which the capital budget for this project was formally authorized through the utility's capital appropriations approval process. Marks the transition from planned to approved status and enables commitment of funds.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; Utility Capital Appropriations Policy

description: Total capital budget amount authorized by the utility's capital appropriations process for this project, expressed in US dollars. Represents the approved spending ceiling for the project. Used for capital program tracking, variance analysis, and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

business_glossary_term: Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) vs Operating Expenditure (OPEX) Split Percentage
description: Percentage of total project costs classified as capital expenditure (CAPEX) versus operating expenditure (OPEX), expressed as the CAPEX percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Supports GAAP capitalization policy compliance and regulatory cost classification for rate case filings.
reference: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

business_glossary_term: Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) Amount
description: Dollar amount of Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) received or expected for this project, expressed in US dollars. Reduces the utility's net capital investment and rate base. Null if ciac_indicator is False.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 980; IRS Revenue Ruling 2007-31

business_glossary_term: Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) Indicator
description: Flag indicating whether this capital project involves a Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) from a customer or developer (True) or not (False). CIAC represents funds or assets contributed by third parties to fund utility infrastructure extensions. Affects rate base treatment and tax accounting under GAAP and FERC rules.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 980; IRS Revenue Ruling 2007-31

description: Date on which the capital project was formally closed in the ERP system, finalizing all cost postings and completing the CWIP-to-plant transfer. Null until the project reaches closed status.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: SAP or ERP cost center code associated with the sponsoring department for this capital project. Used for cost allocation, departmental CAPEX reporting, and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO) Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Timestamp when the capital project record was first created in the source ERP system (SAP PS or Oracle Projects), in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

description: FERC Account 107 (Electric) or Account 105 (Gas) Construction Work in Progress sub-account code used to accumulate project costs prior to in-service date. Supports CWIP balance reporting for rate case filings and regulatory plant additions schedules.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: Annual straight-line depreciation rate applied to the capital project assets upon in-service, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.033333 for 3.33% / 30-year life). Determined by the utility's FERC-approved or PUC-approved depreciation study by asset class. Null until the project is placed in service.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 360; State PUC Depreciation Study Approvals

description: Current forecast of total project cost at completion, expressed in US dollars. Reflects the project manager's latest estimate incorporating actual costs to date plus remaining work. Supports capital program forecasting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account number to which the completed capital project will be classified upon in-service (e.g., Account 101 Electric Plant in Service, Account 107 Construction Work in Progress, Account 303 Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, Account 350 Land and Land Rights - Transmission). Critical for regulatory accounting, rate base calculations, and FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: Fiscal year in which the capital project is primarily budgeted and tracked (e.g., 2024). Used for annual capital program reporting, budget cycle alignment, and year-over-year CAPEX trend analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; GAAP Financial Reporting

description: Flag indicating whether this is a blanket capital project (True) or a specific discrete capital project (False). Blanket projects represent recurring capital programs (e.g., annual pole replacement, annual meter deployment) that aggregate multiple small work orders under a single project authorization. Specific projects represent discrete capital investments with defined scope and budget.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; Utility Capital Program Management

description: Primary business justification category for the capital investment. Used for capital program portfolio analysis and regulatory prudency demonstrations. Values: reliability (grid or system reliability improvement), safety (worker or public safety), regulatory_compliance (mandated by FERC, PUC, EPA, NERC, PHMSA, or OSHA), growth (customer growth or load growth), replacement (end-of-life asset replacement), efficiency (operational efficiency improvement), environmental (environmental remediation or GHG reduction). reference: NERC Reliability Standards; PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations; State PUC Capital Prudency Standards

description: Timestamp when the capital project record was most recently modified in the source ERP system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports change tracking, SOX audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standard
description: NERC reliability standard (e.g., FAC-001, TPL-001, PRC-005) that mandates or drives this capital project, if applicable. Null if the project is not driven by a NERC compliance requirement. Supports regulatory compliance reporting and capital prudency documentation.

Final gross plant addition amount recorded to the FERC plant in service account upon project close-out and in-service transfer, expressed in US dollars. Represents the capitalized cost of the asset placed in service, net of any CIAC. Used for FERC Form 1 plant additions schedule and rate base calculations.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1 Schedule of Plant Additions

description: Numeric priority ranking of the capital project within the utility's annual capital program, used for capital budget allocation and deferral decisions. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Assigned during the annual capital planning cycle.
reference: Utility Capital Program Management; IRP (Integrated Resource Plan)

description: Name of the capital program or portfolio under which this project is grouped (e.g., 'Grid Modernization Program', 'Gas Main Replacement Program', 'AMI Deployment Program'). Supports capital program-level reporting and strategic investment tracking.
reference: Utility Capital Program Management; IRP (Integrated Resource Plan)

description: Detailed narrative description of the capital project scope, including the work to be performed, assets to be installed or replaced, and business justification. Supports rate case cost-of-service studies and regulatory reporting to PUCs and FERC.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

description: Name or employee identifier of the project manager responsible for delivering the capital project on time and within budget. Used for accountability tracking, capital program reporting, and escalation routing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

description: Short human-readable name or title of the capital expenditure project (e.g., 'Substation 12 Transformer Replacement', 'Annual Pole Replacement Program FY2024'). Used in dashboards, capital program reports, and regulatory plant additions filings.

Externally-known alphanumeric project identifier assigned by the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system (e.g., SAP PS WBS element or Oracle Project number). Used for cross-system reference, regulatory filings, and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Date on which capital project activities (design, procurement, or construction) formally commenced. Used for project duration tracking, AFUDC accrual period calculation, and capital program scheduling.

Current lifecycle status of the capital expenditure project. Drives capital program prioritization, CWIP balance reporting, and regulatory plant additions reporting. Values: planned (identified but not yet authorized), approved (capital budget authorized), in_progress (construction or implementation underway), complete (work finished, pending close-out), closed (fully closed and placed in service or written off), cancelled (project terminated prior to completion).
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Functional classification of the capital project by utility business segment. Used for capital program segmentation, regulatory reporting, and rate base allocation. Values: transmission (high-voltage bulk electric infrastructure), distribution (last-mile electric delivery), generation (power plant assets), gas (natural gas pipeline and distribution), it (information technology infrastructure), environmental_compliance (environmental or regulatory compliance investments).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Capital Reporting Requirements

description: Regulatory jurisdiction governing the capital project for rate base and cost recovery purposes. Values: ferc (subject to FERC jurisdiction, e.g., transmission assets), state_puc (subject to state Public Utility Commission jurisdiction, e.g., distribution assets), both (dual jurisdiction), exempt (not subject to rate regulation).
reference: FERC (18 CFR); State PUC Tariff and Rate Case Rules

description: Most recent revised authorized budget amount reflecting approved budget amendments or change orders since original authorization. Null if no revisions have been approved. Supports capital program variance reporting and rate case prudency reviews.
reference: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

description: Geographic service territory or operating division within which the capital project is located (e.g., Northern Region, Southern Region, Metro District). Used for geographic capital program analysis and regulatory jurisdiction reporting.
reference: State PUC Service Territory Definitions; ESRI ArcGIS GIS

description: Flag indicating whether this capital project is subject to Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) internal controls over financial reporting (True) or not (False). SOX-relevant projects require documented approval workflows, segregation of duties, and audit trail maintenance per SOX Section 302 and 404 requirements.
reference: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Sections 302 and 404; GAAP Internal Controls

description: Name or code of the utility business department or organizational unit sponsoring and accountable for the capital project (e.g., Transmission Engineering, Distribution Operations, Gas Operations, IT). Used for capital program allocation and departmental CAPEX reporting.

Planned date on which the capital project assets are expected to be placed in service and transferred from Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) to plant in service accounts. Drives capital program scheduling, AFUDC cessation planning, and regulatory plant additions forecasting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module

description: Work Breakdown Structure element code that hierarchically organizes the capital project within the utility's capital program. Aligns with SAP PS WBS element or Oracle Projects task structure for cost collection and CWIP balance reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

reference: SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting (FI-AA) — Depreciation Run (AFAB)

reference: PUC Depreciation Study Requirements; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC
