Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: depreciation_run has gl_account_code attribute. gl_account is the master for GL accounts. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full account details (account_name, ferc_account_description,

Total accumulated depreciation balance (in USD) for the assets processed in this run as of the end of the fiscal period, across the specified depreciation area. Represents the cumulative depreciation charged against the gross plant-in-service balance. Used in FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 and rate base calculations for rate cases.
reference: FERC Form 1 Schedule 336; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108

description: Timestamp when the depreciation run was approved for posting by the authorized finance approver. Part of the SOX audit trail for the depreciation posting lifecycle.
reference: SOX Section 404; GAAP Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICFR)

description: User ID or name of the finance manager or controller who approved the depreciation run for posting. Supports SOX segregation of duties controls requiring that the person who initiates a depreciation run is different from the person who approves it.
reference: SOX Section 404; GAAP Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICFR)

description: FERC or ERP asset class code identifying the category of fixed assets included in this depreciation run (e.g., '301' = Organization, '303' = Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, '350' = Land and Land Rights, '353' = Station Equipment, '362' = Meters, '391' = Office Furniture). Aligns with FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account codes. If the run covers all asset classes, this field is null.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101 — Electric Plant Accounts 301–399; Gas Plant Accounts 101–399

description: Number of fixed asset records that encountered errors and were excluded from depreciation calculation during this run. A non-zero value requires investigation and potential rerun. Supports SOX completeness controls over the depreciation process.

Total number of fixed asset records processed during this depreciation run. Used for run completeness validation, reconciliation against the fixed asset register count, and identifying partial runs or processing errors.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; SOX Section 404 (completeness assertion)

description: SAP company code or ERP legal entity identifier representing the regulated utility entity (e.g., electric operating company, gas distribution company) for which the depreciation run was executed. Supports multi-entity utility holding company structures and separate FERC/PUC regulatory reporting by legal entity.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 810

description: Timestamp when this depreciation run record was first captured in the data platform. Used for audit trail and SOX compliance over the depreciation posting process.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the depreciation amounts in this run (e.g., 'USD'). Supports multi-currency reporting for utility holding companies with international operations.

Code identifying the depreciation valuation area for which this run was executed. Common utility depreciation areas: '01' = Book/GAAP, '10' = Federal Tax (MACRS), '15' = State Tax, '20' = Regulatory/FERC, '30' = Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT), '40' = Group/Composite. Each area maintains independent depreciation values per SAP FI-AA configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 01|10|15|20|30|40 — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA Depreciation Areas; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; IRS MACRS Publication 946

description: Human-readable name of the depreciation area (e.g., 'Book/GAAP', 'Federal Tax MACRS', 'State Tax', 'Regulatory/FERC', 'Alternative Minimum Tax', 'Group/Composite'). Supports reporting and audit trail readability without requiring a join to a reference table.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Code identifying the depreciation calculation method applied during this run. 'SL' = Straight-Line (primary GAAP method for utilities); 'GRP' = Group/Composite (common for utility plant accounts per FERC); 'SYD' = Sum-of-Years-Digits; 'DB' = Declining Balance; 'UOP' = Units-of-Production. Determines the mathematical basis for depreciation expense calculation.
reference: GAAP ASC 360-10; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101; IRS Publication 946

description: Full descriptive name of the depreciation method applied (e.g., 'Straight-Line', 'Group/Composite', 'Sum-of-Years-Digits', 'Declining Balance', 'Units-of-Production'). Supports FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 reporting and rate case cost-of-service documentation.

The composite or average depreciation rate (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.033333 for 3.3333%) applied during this run. For group/composite depreciation, this is the PUC-approved composite rate from the most recent depreciation study. For straight-line, this is the reciprocal of the average service life. Key parameter for depreciation study true-up analysis.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Depreciation Study; GAAP ASC 360

description: Indicates whether the depreciation rates applied in this run are interim rates (provisionally approved by the PUC pending final order), final rates (approved in a final PUC order), proposed rates (filed but not yet approved), or approved rates (in effect under current tariff). Critical for regulatory accounting and rate case true-up calculations.
reference: PUC Depreciation Study Requirements; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC

description: System-generated error message text when run_status = 'error'. Captures the ERP error description to support troubleshooting and resolution of failed depreciation runs. Null when the run completed successfully.

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account number to which the depreciation expense from this run is attributed (e.g., '403' = Depreciation Expense — Electric, '404' = Amortization of Limited-Term Electric Plant). Required for FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 depreciation and amortization reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336

description: The accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year to which this depreciation run applies. Determines the general ledger period into which depreciation expense is posted.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA

description: The fiscal year (four-digit integer, e.g., 2024) to which this depreciation run applies. Aligns with the utility's GAAP and FERC regulatory accounting fiscal year for financial statement preparation and FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336

description: Total gross plant-in-service value (in USD) of the assets processed in this depreciation run as of the run date. Represents the depreciable asset base. Used to validate the depreciation rate applied (total_depreciation_amount / gross_plant_amount) and supports rate base calculations in rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 360; PUC Rate Case Cost-of-Service

description: Indicates whether this run is a repeat execution for a period that was previously processed (True) or a first-time run for the period (False). Repeat runs occur after reversals or corrections. Relevant for SOX controls over duplicate depreciation postings.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; SOX Section 404

description: Indicates whether this depreciation run was executed in simulation (test) mode without posting to the general ledger (True) or as a live posting run (False). Simulation runs are used to preview depreciation amounts before period-end close.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; SOX Section 404

description: Free-text notes entered by the run initiator or approver describing the purpose, scope, or any exceptions associated with this depreciation run (e.g., 'Year-end true-up run applying final PUC-approved rates from Docket 2024-001', 'Repeat run after reversal of period 6 posting error').

The budgeted or planned depreciation amount for this fiscal period and depreciation area, as established in the depreciation study or annual budget. Compared against total_depreciation_amount to identify variances for depreciation study true-up analysis and rate case cost-of-service reconciliation.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; PUC Depreciation Study Requirements

description: The date on which the depreciation amounts were posted to the general ledger. May differ from run_date if the run was simulated first and posted later. Critical for period-end close cutoff and GAAP accrual accounting.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; SOX Section 404

description: ERP financial document number (e.g., SAP FI document number) generated when depreciation amounts are posted to the general ledger. Provides the audit trail linkage between the depreciation run and the actual GL posting for SOX compliance and external audit support.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; GAAP ASC 360

description: The date on which the depreciation run posting was reversed in the general ledger. Null if not reversed. Used in conjunction with reversal_document_number to track corrected depreciation entries.
reference: GAAP ASC 250; SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA

description: ERP financial document number of the reversal posting if this depreciation run was reversed. Null if the run has not been reversed. Supports audit trail for corrected depreciation postings and SOX compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 250 (Accounting Changes and Error Corrections)

description: The calendar date on which the depreciation calculation run was executed. This is the principal business event date — the date the depreciation program was triggered in the asset accounting system.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; GAAP ASC 360

description: Timestamp when the depreciation calculation program completed execution. Used with run_start_timestamp to measure total processing duration for operational monitoring of the period-end close process.

User ID or system account that initiated the depreciation run in the ERP system. Required for SOX audit trail to establish accountability over the depreciation posting process and segregation of duties compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP Internal Controls

description: Externally-known business identifier assigned to the depreciation run by the ERP system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA depreciation run document number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail reference.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Timestamp when the depreciation calculation program began execution in the ERP system. Used with run_end_timestamp to measure processing duration and identify performance issues with large asset portfolios.

Current lifecycle state of the depreciation run. 'planned' indicates scheduled but not yet executed; 'simulated' indicates a test run without posting; 'posted' indicates amounts have been committed to the general ledger; 'reversed' indicates the posting has been reversed; 'error' indicates the run failed during processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Classification of the depreciation run by its business purpose. 'periodic' = standard monthly/quarterly run; 'year_end' = annual closing run; 'special' = off-cycle run for asset disposals or acquisitions; 'repeat' = rerun of a previously executed period.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; GAAP ASC 360

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this depreciation run record was sourced (e.g., 'SAP_S4', 'ORACLE_ERP'). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; Oracle ERP Cloud Fixed Assets

description: Total depreciation expense amount (in USD) calculated and posted during this run across all assets processed. This is the gross depreciation charge for the period and depreciation area. Key input for rate case cost-of-service calculations, FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 reporting, and GAAP income statement depreciation expense line.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Timestamp when this depreciation run record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks status changes such as reversal or error correction for SOX audit trail.
Primary key for depreciation_study
Self-referencing FK on depreciation_study (prior_depreciation_study_id)
Reference to the previous depreciation study that this study supersedes or updates. Nullable for initial studies.
Total accumulated depreciation reserve for all assets in the study scope as of the study analysis date, measured in US dollars.
Statistical method used to estimate service life and survivor characteristics of asset groups. Iowa curves are industry standard for utility depreciation studies.
Projected annual depreciation expense resulting from the rates recommended in this study, measured in US dollars.
Date when the regulatory body officially approved the depreciation study and its recommended rates. Nullable for pending or internal studies.
Official order or decision number issued by the regulatory body approving the depreciation study. Nullable for unapproved studies.
Total gross plant value (original cost) of all assets included in the scope of this depreciation study, measured in US dollars.
Weighted average remaining service life for existing assets in the study scope, measured in years.
Weighted average estimated service life across all asset classes included in the study, measured in years.
Name of the external consulting firm that prepared or assisted with the depreciation study. Nullable if study was performed entirely in-house.
Timestamp when this depreciation study record was first created in the system.

Primary depreciation calculation methodology applied in this study. Straight-line is most common for utility assets under FERC guidelines. Remaining life and equal life group methods are used for mass property accounts.
Date when the depreciation rates and parameters from this study become effective for accounting and regulatory purposes.
Date when the depreciation study parameters are scheduled to be superseded by a new study. Nullable for studies with indefinite applicability.
Date when the depreciation study was officially filed with the regulatory body. Nullable for internal studies.
Official docket or case number assigned by the regulatory body when the depreciation study is filed for approval. Nullable for internal studies not requiring regulatory filing.
Flag indicating whether the depreciation study methodology and rates comply with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. True for studies used in GAAP financial reporting.
Timestamp when this depreciation study record was most recently updated in the system.
Name of the primary analyst or actuary responsible for conducting the depreciation study.
Net plant value (gross plant minus accumulated depreciation) for all assets in the study scope, measured in US dollars.

Weighted average net salvage value as a percentage of original cost across all asset classes. Net salvage represents gross salvage minus cost of removal. Can be negative when removal costs exceed salvage value.
Additional notes, comments, or special considerations related to the depreciation study, including any deviations from standard methodology or unique circumstances.
Docket number of the associated rate case if this study was prepared for rate case purposes. Nullable if not associated with a rate case.
Flag indicating whether this depreciation study was prepared specifically to support a rate case filing. True if study is part of rate case, false otherwise.
Name of the specific regulatory agency or commission that has jurisdiction over this depreciation study (e.g., FERC, state public utility commission name).

Primary regulatory jurisdiction governing this depreciation study. Federal studies follow FERC guidelines, state studies follow public utility commission requirements, and multi-jurisdictional studies address multiple regulatory bodies.
Flag indicating whether this depreciation study was subject to Sarbanes-Oxley internal control requirements and review. True for studies affecting financial statements of publicly traded utilities.
Date when the depreciation study analysis was completed and finalized for submission or approval.
File path or URL to the complete depreciation study report and supporting documentation in the document management system.
Descriptive name of the depreciation study, typically including the asset class or scope covered.
Business identifier for the depreciation study, typically formatted as DS-YYYY-NNNN where YYYY is year and NNNN is sequence number.
Detailed description of the asset classes, FERC accounts, and organizational units covered by this depreciation study.
Date when the depreciation study analysis and data collection commenced.
Current lifecycle status of the depreciation study. Tracks progression from initial draft through regulatory approval and implementation.

Classification of the depreciation study based on scope and purpose. Comprehensive studies cover all asset classes, interim studies update specific parameters, special studies address unique circumstances, rate case studies support regulatory filings, and asset class specific studies focus on particular equipment categories.
Unique surrogate identifier for the fixed asset record in the financial subledger. Primary key for the fixed_asset data product.

Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: fixed_asset is capitalized from CAPEX projects. The cwip_transfer_reference and wbs_element attributes suggest a link to the originating project. This FK allows tracing each asset back to its capital

Cross-reference identifier linking this financial fixed asset record to the corresponding operational asset record in the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo). Enables reconciliation between the financial subledger and the operational asset register for asset lifecycle management and maintenance cost tracking.
reference: Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Fixed assets track original vendor for warranty claims, maintenance contracts, spare parts sourcing, and asset provenance. Essential for asset lifecycle management, vendor performance tracking, and re

Total depreciation accrued on the asset from in-service date through the current reporting period. Represents the cumulative reduction in the asset's book value due to wear, obsolescence, and passage of time. Used to compute net book value and rate base. Denominated in USD. Corresponds to FERC Account 108 (Accumulated Provision for Depreciation of Electric Utility Plant) or equivalent gas accounts.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 219

description: Date on which the utility acquired ownership or control of the asset (purchase date, transfer date, or contribution date). May differ from in-service date for assets acquired from third parties or contributed by developers (CIAC — Contribution in Aid of Construction).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Amount
description: Total Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) capitalized into the original cost of this asset during the construction period. AFUDC represents the cost of debt and equity capital used to finance construction before the asset is placed in service. Regulated by FERC and included in rate base. Denominated in USD.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Accounts 107, 432, 436; GAAP ASC 835-20; FERC Form 1

description: The composite or straight-line annual depreciation rate applied to this asset or asset group, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.033333 for a 30-year life). Derived from the FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Used to compute annual depreciation expense for regulatory reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336

description: Internal asset classification grouping used for depreciation study purposes and rate case cost-of-service analysis (e.g., Transmission Structure, Distribution Transformer, Gas Meter, Generation Turbine, Intangible Software). Maps to depreciation group/composite rates established in the most recent depreciation study approved by the state PUC or FERC.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 360

description: Human-readable description of the capitalized utility plant asset (e.g., '138kV Transmission Line Segment — Substation A to Substation B', 'Gas Distribution Main — 4-inch PE Pipe'). Sourced from the asset master record in the ERP fixed asset module.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360

description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the capitalized asset in the fixed asset subledger (e.g., SAP S/4HANA Asset Master number or Oracle ERP asset number). Used for cross-system reconciliation between the financial subledger and the operational asset register in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Recorded Asset Retirement Obligation (ARO) associated with this asset, representing the present value of the estimated future cost to retire the asset in accordance with legal or regulatory obligations (e.g., nuclear decommissioning, PCB-contaminated equipment disposal, gas main abandonment). Recognized per GAAP ASC 410-20 and tracked for FERC regulatory accounting. Denominated in USD.
reference: GAAP ASC 410-20; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 230; EPA Regulations; PHMSA

description: Current lifecycle status of the fixed asset in the utility plant subledger. 'in_service' indicates the asset is placed in service and included in rate base. 'cwip' indicates Construction Work in Progress not yet transferred to plant in service. 'retired' indicates the asset has been removed from service. Aligns with FERC plant account status classifications.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10

description: Broad classification of the asset as tangible utility plant, intangible plant, or Construction Work in Progress (CWIP). Tangible includes physical generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure. Intangible includes software, licenses, and franchise rights. CWIP represents assets not yet placed in service.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 350; GAAP ASC 360

description: Strategic CAPEX category classifying the business driver for the capital investment in this asset. 'growth' supports customer or load growth. 'reliability' improves grid or system reliability (SAIDI/SAIFI improvement). 'compliance' meets regulatory or environmental mandates. 'replacement' replaces end-of-life infrastructure. 'technology' supports grid modernization or AMI deployment. Used in IRP and regulatory filings.
reference: FERC Form 1; IRP Regulatory Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC CAPEX Filings

description: Minimum dollar threshold applied to determine whether an expenditure on this asset class is capitalized as plant in service or expensed as O&M. Established by the utility's capitalization policy, approved by the board, and subject to SOX internal controls. Denominated in USD.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

business_glossary_term: Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) Amount
description: Amount of Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) received from customers, developers, or third parties that offset the original cost of this asset. CIAC reduces the rate base for regulatory purposes. Tracked per FERC Account 271 and applicable state PUC tariff rules. Denominated in USD.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 271; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; IRS Revenue Ruling 2020-23

description: Actual or estimated cost incurred to remove the asset from service upon retirement (excavation, demolition, environmental remediation, disposal). Subtracted from gross salvage to determine net salvage. Frequently exceeds gross salvage for underground utility infrastructure, resulting in negative net salvage. Denominated in USD.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108.1; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 410

business_glossary_term: Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) Transfer Reference
description: Reference number or identifier of the Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) work order or project from which this asset was transferred upon completion and placement in service. Links the capitalized plant record back to the capital project that funded its construction. Corresponds to FERC Account 107 (Construction Work in Progress) transfer transactions.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

description: Code identifying the depreciation group or composite account to which this asset belongs for group/composite depreciation purposes. Assets within the same depreciation group share a common composite depreciation rate derived from the FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Critical for utility industry group depreciation accounting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 360-10-35-7

description: Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation expense for this asset. 'straight_line' allocates cost evenly over useful life. 'group_composite' is the predominant utility industry method where assets are depreciated as a group using composite rates derived from depreciation studies approved by FERC or state PUCs. 'units_of_production' is used for generation assets tied to output.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10-35; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines

description: The year of the most recent FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study from which the depreciation rates, useful life, and net salvage rate for this asset class were derived. Depreciation studies are typically conducted every 3–5 years and filed with the applicable regulatory authority. Tracks which study vintage governs the current depreciation parameters.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; State PUC Depreciation Study Orders

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account code to which this asset is classified (e.g., 101 Electric Plant in Service, 303 Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, 350 Land and Land Rights — Transmission, 376 Distribution Mains — Gas). Drives FERC Form 1 plant schedule reporting (Schedules 204–207) and rate base calculations.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1 Schedules 204–207

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account Name
description: Descriptive name corresponding to the FERC plant account code (e.g., 'Electric Plant in Service', 'Distribution Mains — Gas'). Supports human-readable reporting on FERC Form 1 plant schedules without requiring a join to a reference table.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101)

description: FERC functional classification of the utility plant asset: Generation, Transmission, Distribution, General Plant, or Intangible. Drives allocation of rate base and O&M costs across customer classes in rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: Actual or estimated gross salvage proceeds received or expected upon retirement of the asset (scrap value, resale proceeds). Used in conjunction with cost of removal to compute net salvage for depreciation study updates. Populated upon retirement; null for in-service assets. Denominated in USD.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 360-10-40

description: Date on which the asset was placed in service and began depreciating. Triggers the start of depreciation accrual and inclusion in the utility rate base. For CWIP-to-plant transfers, this is the date the CWIP balance is transferred to plant in service. Critical for AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) cessation.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 204

description: Indicates whether this asset is eligible for inclusion in the utility's regulatory rate base for cost-of-service rate case purposes. Assets funded by CIAC, regulatory disallowances, or held for future use may be excluded from rate base. Critical for PUC and FERC rate case filings.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; State PUC Regulations

description: Indicates whether this item is classified as a regulatory asset under GAAP ASC 980 (Regulated Operations), meaning its recovery through future rates is probable. Regulatory assets arise from costs deferred for rate recovery (e.g., storm damage costs, deferred fuel costs, environmental remediation). Affects balance sheet presentation and rate case strategy.
reference: GAAP ASC 980; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Regulations

description: Date of the most recent physical inventory verification confirming the existence and condition of this asset. Physical inventories are required for SOX compliance (internal controls over financial reporting) and support reconciliation between the fixed asset subledger and the operational asset register in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Code identifying the physical or operational location of the asset within the utility's service territory (e.g., substation identifier, distribution circuit code, gas pressure zone, plant site code). Used for geographic cost allocation in rate cases and for reconciliation with the GIS (ESRI ArcGIS) asset network model.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; ESRI ArcGIS GIS Integration; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

description: Current net book value of the asset, calculated as original cost minus accumulated depreciation. Represents the carrying value of the asset on the utility's balance sheet and is the primary basis for rate base inclusion in cost-of-service rate cases. Denominated in USD. Note: while derivable, this field is stored for performance and regulatory reporting efficiency.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

description: The net salvage rate applied to this asset class in the depreciation study, expressed as a decimal. Net salvage equals gross salvage proceeds minus cost of removal. For utility assets, net salvage is frequently negative (negative salvage) because cost of removal (e.g., pole removal, underground cable excavation, gas main abandonment) exceeds any scrap value. Negative salvage rates increase the depreciable base and are a critical input unique to utility depreciation studies.
reference: NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Iowa Curve Methodology

description: The original cost of the utility plant asset at the time it was first dedicated to public service, as defined by FERC Uniform System of Accounts. Includes all costs necessary to bring the asset to its intended use (materials, labor, AFUDC, overhead). This is the FERC-defined original cost, not necessarily the acquisition cost paid by the current owner. Denominated in USD.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1 Schedule 204; GAAP ASC 360

description: Timestamp when this fixed asset record was first created in the financial subledger system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Supports SOX audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Timestamp when this fixed asset record was most recently modified in the financial subledger system. Tracks changes to depreciation parameters, status updates, retirement entries, and cost adjustments. Supports SOX audit trail and Silver Layer change data capture (CDC) processing.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Estimated remaining useful service life of the asset in years as of the most recent depreciation study or valuation date. Computed as useful life minus age (years since in-service date), adjusted for condition assessments. Used in rate case depreciation studies, IRP capital planning, and asset replacement forecasting.
reference: NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Iowa Curve Methodology

description: Date on which the asset was retired, abandoned, or removed from utility plant in service. Triggers cessation of depreciation accrual and removal from rate base. Null for assets currently in service. Required for FERC Form 1 plant retirement schedules.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10-40; FERC Form 1 Schedule 205

description: Classification of the asset retirement event. 'normal' retirements are expected end-of-life removals consistent with the depreciation study survivor curve. 'abnormal' retirements are premature removals due to accidents, storms, or regulatory mandates. 'extraordinary' retirements involve large-scale plant abandonments. Classification affects regulatory accounting treatment and potential regulatory asset recovery.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10-40; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines

description: Name or code of the regulatory service territory or jurisdiction in which the asset is located (e.g., state name, PUC jurisdiction code). Determines which state Public Utility Commission (PUC) has regulatory jurisdiction over the asset's rate base treatment and depreciation rates.
reference: State PUC Regulations; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC
